title: AutoEncoder-Compressed Parallel Split Learning for Pre-Trained Model Fine-Tuning
description: Split learning moves computation off edge devices, but exchanging activations and gradients at every step can overwhelm the network. AE-PSL aligns a lightweight autoencoder with a pre-trained vision model and then with each client’s data, so distributed fine-tuning can exchange compact representations while preserving useful features.

title: Domain Adaptive Pretraining in Split Learning for Vision Foundation Models
description: SDAPT adapts a shared vision foundation model to unlabeled domain images. Frozen client layers keep local computation light; server-side self-distillation learns a common representation, then each client trains its own task head.

title: EFU: Enforcing Federated Unlearning via Functional Encryption
description: A server should not silently drop an unlearning update from the agreed federated aggregation. EFU binds encrypted updates to authorized aggregation and lets clients submit learning or unlearning updates through the same protocol. Its experiments measure the trade-off between forgetting selected information and retaining model utility.

title: EncCluster: Scalable Functional Encryption in Federated Learning through Weight Clustering and Probabilistic Filters
description: Secure aggregation can make federated learning expensive for devices with limited compute and bandwidth. EncCluster clusters model weights before functional encryption, then encodes the weight-to-cluster mappings with probabilistic filters, reducing the amount of data that must be encrypted and transmitted while allowing the server to reconstruct encrypted updates for aggregation.

title: Many-Task Federated Fine-Tuning via Unified Task Vectors
description: Federated clients may work on several different tasks, making a single averaged model a poor fit. MaTU combines each client’s task updates into one unified vector with lightweight masks and scaling factors, then uses task similarity to share useful updates across clients while limiting interference between unrelated tasks.

title: Fine-Tuning Multimodal Transformers on Edge: A Parallel Split Learning Approach
description: Multimodal transformers are expensive to fine-tune on edge devices, even when only a small fraction of their parameters changes. MPSL keeps modality-specific tokenizers on clients and moves a shared encoder to the server, coordinating learning through aggregated local losses while supporting different combinations of images, audio and text.

title: DeltaMask: Minimizing Communication in Federated Fine-Tuning of Vision Foundation Models
description: Large vision models make federated updates costly, even when compressed to one bit per parameter. DeltaMask keeps pre-trained weights fixed and learns stochastic masks, then communicates selected changes through compact probabilistic filters so clients can collaborate at a fraction of the bitrate of a full binary mask.

title: FedCode: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning via Transferring Codebooks
description: Even compressed model updates can overwhelm a federated learning link when the full update is sent every round. FedCode exchanges compact codebooks of weight-cluster centers in most rounds, periodically transferring compressed weights to realign client and server models. Clients cluster all model weights together in a model-wide step.

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning through Adaptive Weight Clustering and Server-Side Distillation
description: Compressing client updates alone leaves the aggregated server model expensive to send back. FedCompress clusters weights during local training and restores a compact global model through server-side distillation, using unlabeled data and a representation-quality signal to adapt compression as learning progresses without changing the underlying aggregation rule.

title: Labeling Chaos to Learning Harmony: Federated Learning with Noisy Labels
description: Federated clients have different amounts of label noise and different computational budgets. FedLN estimates noise on each client and offers three ways to limit its influence: correcting labels before training, adding adaptive knowledge distillation during local learning, or adjusting server aggregation to place more weight on reliable updates.

title: On the Effectiveness of Invisible Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning
description: A visually subtle trigger does not behave the same way in centralized and federated training. This study examines how limited local training, competing client updates, and server-side defenses affect invisible backdoor attacks, then investigates whether placing triggers in regions receiving little model attention changes attack success and detectability.

title: On efficacy of Meta-Learning for Domain Generalization in Speech Emotion Recognition
description: Models that recognize emotion in one speech dataset often fail on another. This study evaluates domain-shift-aware meta-learning for speech emotion recognition, finds mixed gains with log-mel inputs, and tests whether stronger acoustic representations improve held-out-domain performance.

title: Plug-and-Play Multilingual Few-shot Spoken Words Recognition
description: Adding new voice commands usually requires new labeled data and task-specific training. PLiX learns a multilingual audio embedding from millions of one-second clips across 20 languages, then recognizes unseen spoken words by comparing them with prototypes formed from a few support examples, without retraining the model for each new vocabulary.

title: Privacy-preserving Speech Emotion Recognition through Semi-Supervised Federated Learning
description: Speech emotion recognition depends on sensitive audio that is costly to annotate. This work combines an attention-based speech model with federated self-training, using labeled clips and confident predictions on unlabeled clips while keeping raw audio on each device, then studies label scarcity and speaker distribution in IEMOCAP experiments.

title: Federated Self-training for Semi-supervised Audio Recognition
description: Most audio collected on personal devices has no labels, limiting what supervised federated learning can use. FedSTAR combines local self-training with federated aggregation: clients learn from labeled clips and confident predictions on unlabeled clips, while optional self-supervised pre-training supplies a stronger starting point for faster convergence across training rounds.
